item.title: Man Utd & Arsenal eye Croatia striker - Sunday's gossip
item.description: Three Premier League clubs are interested in Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic, Juventus want Liverpool centre-back Giovanni Leoni, Newcastle willing to let Joe Willock leave in January, plus more.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Three Premier League clubs are interested in Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic, Juventus want Liverpool centre-back Giovanni Leoni, Newcastle willing to let Joe Willock leave in January.

Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea are on a growing list of clubs checking on Freiburg's Croatian striker Igor Matanovic, 23. (Caughtoffside), external

Juventus want Liverpool defender Giovanni Leoni, 19, as the Serie A side look to bolster the number of Italian players in their squad. (Gazzetta dello Sport - in Italian), external

Newcastle United are open to letting Joe Willock, 27, leave in the January transfer window, with his contract due to run out in the summer and the English midfielder yet to open negotiations over a new deal. (Football Insider), external

Tottenham have no plans to sell defender Micky van de Ven, 25, as Liverpool prepare to move for the Netherlands international next year. (Football Insider), external

AC Milan are considering a move for Brighton's Sweden midfielder Yasin Ayari, 22, as a possible replacement for Luka Modric, should the 41-year-old Croatia international choose to retire. (Tuttosport via Football Italia), external

Brighton and Bournemouth sent scouts to Medellin to watch 21-year-old Colombian centre-back Neider Parra who plays in his homeland for Atletico Nacional. (El Deportivo - in Spanish), external

Brighton chief executive Paul Barber has plans in place if the team's top performers are targeted by bigger clubs. (Sky Sports), external

Brentford's Icelandic goalkeeper Hakon Rafn Valdimarsson, 24, would consider leaving the club in the future if first-team opportunities continue to be limited. (RUV - in Icelandic), external

Roma want to sign Brazil striker Endrick on loan from Real Madrid in January, with the 20-year-old keen on the move to the Serie A club to get more game time. (Corriere dello Sport - in Italian), external

Barcelona's Brazilian forward Raphinha, 29, and Spanish defender Xavi Espart and midfielder Marc Bernal, both 19, are all in line to sign new contracts with the Catalan club. (Fabrizio Romano), external

item.title: Wakefield beat Warrington to win Super League
item.description: Wakefield Trinity end a 58-year wait to be champions as they claim a deserved Grand Final success over Warrington Wolves at Old Trafford.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Betfred Super League Grand Final

Warrington (0) 10

Tries: Lindop 2 Goals: Irwin

Wakefield (19) 23

Tries: Scott, Vagana, Tevaga, Johnstone Goals: Jowitt 3 Drop goal: Sinfield

Wakefield Trinity became only the sixth, and most unlikely, club to win the Super League title after a deserved win over Warrington Wolves.

Only two years after being in the Championship and in their first ever Grand Final, Wakefield took to the Old Trafford stage as if they were to the manor born.

Daryl Powell's side did the bulk of the damage in a devastating first half as they raced into a 19-0 lead on their way to becoming champions of England for the first time since 1968, long before the Super League era.

Trinity carried on from where they had left off in the semi-final against Wigan Warriors with tries from Cameron Scott, Isaiah Vagana and Jazz Tevaga and a drop goal from Jack Sinfield.

Arron Lindop's try gave Warrington brief hope early in the second half, but when Tom Johnstone went over at the other end, the game was up despite Lindop's second try late on.

Wakefield guarantee legendary status

This is a final few would have predicted seven days ago, let alone at any point throughout the season.

But Warrington snuck past Leeds Rhinos, and Wakefield Trinity then stunned the whole of rugby league as they demolished Wigan on the Warriors' own patch to make it to Old Trafford.

While Warrington have been close in previous years, Wakefield have been spectacular bolters in 2026.

Only two years ago, they were winning the Championship play-off final before their place in Super League was confirmed by the IMG grading system, having been relegated in 2023.

They were sixth last year and went two places better this season before memorable play-off successes over Leigh Leopards and then the Warriors.

Powell had challenged his players to earn legendary status, knowing that was their long-term reward if they could emerge victorious.

After scoring 33 unanswered points in a spell at Wigan, Wakefield simply brought that momentum with them to Old Trafford as they absolutely bossed the first half, stretching that streak to 52 points.

Johnstone had already had one try denied by a TV review before Lachlan Walmsley's brilliant reverse pass sent Scott over to score.

And in a period where everything they did was working, Jake Trueman's high kick on the last tackle was spectacularly caught by Johnstone above opposite wing Albert Hopoate and tapped back for the supporting Vagana to dive over.

They were overpowering their opponents, exemplified by Tevaga being unstoppable from close to the posts for their third try.

And showing the sort of game smarts his revered father Sir Kevin Sinfield had in his Leeds Rhinos days, Jack Sinfield added an extra point to keep the scoreboard ticking as the half closed to leave Warrington needing more than three converted tries.

Warrington bridesmaids for a fifth time

In the Super League era, Warrington have been the eternal bridesmaids, watching on as traditional rivals Wigan and St Helens have swept up the silverware.

This was their fifth Grand Final, and felt like the chance to finally get their hands on the big prize and be champions for the first time since 1955.

Under head coach Sam Burgess, they had lost Challenge Cup finals at Wembley in the previous two years, but they had arrived at this game on the back of nine wins out of 10.

Crucially that sole defeat had been at Wakefield in round 26 of the regular season and in the opening 40 minutes, they had few answers.

But a high tackle by Trinity centre Corey Hall resulted in him being sin-binned early in the second period and, with a man extra, Lindop went over to offer a glimmer of a comeback.

However, Warrington could not score again with that momentum. Wakefield weathered the storm and, with numbers levelled up, they worked an opening for Johnstone's power and pace to deliver the decisive try.

Lindop went over again for his second as the Wolves desperately attacked, but with Ewan Irwin missing the conversion, Trinity players and staff were able to count down until the final whistle before celebrations could begin as Warrington's wait for another title now extends to a 72nd year.

Interchanges: Lino, Potts, Faatili, Hamlin-Uele.

Sin-bin: Hall (43)

Referee: Liam Moore.

item.title: Ronaldo 'greatest symbol' of Portugal - Fernandes
item.description: Portugal midfielder Bruno Fernandes says Cristiano Ronaldo remains the country's greatest footballing figure despite leaving the squad this week after finding out he would not start a match.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Portugal midfielder Bruno Fernandes said Cristiano Ronaldo remains the country's greatest footballing figure despite leaving the squad this week after finding out he would not start a match.

Ronaldo, 41, left after coach Jorge Jesus said he would not start against Denmark in the Nations League, a match Portugal won 4-2 without him.

The former Real Madrid and Manchester United forward has scored 146 goals from 234 matches with Portugal - both record figures - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice.

However, his international future now appears to be in doubt.

Manchester United's Fernandes, speaking at a Portugal news conference on Saturday, said: "Regarding Cristiano, I had a conversation with him.

"What I told him, and what I repeat here, is regardless of what happens, Cristiano Ronaldo will never cease to be the greatest symbol of our national team, of our football, and of the country, for what he has done not only in Portugal but throughout the world.

"He has a reserved place not only among the best of all time, but also in the hearts of all Portuguese people, and the most important thing is that we stop dividing things.

"There are no divisions in the national team. It is one and will remain so, despite any noise that may come from outside.

"We are outside of this controversy, but what I ask is that the country does not divide itself, does not make choices, that it respects all sides. Cris is and will be the biggest icon of our national team, he deserves everyone's respect, regardless of who likes him more or [who likes him] less."

Portugal won the Nations League in 2019 and are the current holders after they beat Spain in the 2025 final on penalties, following a 2-2 draw in which Ronaldo scored one of his team's goals.

They reached the last 16 of this summer's World Cup, before losing 1-0 to eventual champions Spain, although then manager Roberto Martinez was criticised for rarely substituting Ronaldo, even if he was playing poorly.

Jesus, who had been Ronaldo's club manager at Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr, replaced Martinez for the Nations League campaign.

Portugal began with a 1-0 home win over Wales, with Ronaldo playing the opening 67 minutes, but he was an unused substitute in the 2-1 away victory over Norway and then left the squad before the Denmark game.

After three matches, Portugal are top of Group A4 with nine points from nine and play Norway at home on Sunday.

They end the group phase next month, with a home match against Denmark on 14 November followed by a game in Wales on 17 November.

If they finish in the top two in the section, they would qualify for the quarter-finals in March, before the semi-finals and final are held in June.

Coach Jesus said Ronaldo was a "symbol of Portugal" and said there would be time to speak about him after Sunday's game in Porto.

"I'm going to focus on the team, on the opponent which is Norway, one of the five best teams in Europe. That's the problem right now," said the 72-year-old coach.

item.title: England's Jordan in contention at Alfred Dunhill Links
item.description: England's Matthew Jordan is two shots off the lead heading into the final round of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Alfred Dunhill Links Championship - round three

-18 C Jarvis (SA); -16 M Jordan (Eng); -15 T Detry (Bel); -14 A Meronk (Pol), N Norgaard (Den), J Skov Olesen (Den)

Selected others: -13 M Armitage (Eng); -12 M Fitzpatrick (Eng), -11 R MacIntyre (Sco), C Hill (Sco), -10 S Bairstow (Eng), R Mansell (Eng), D Brown (Eng), C Syme (Sco), M Stewart (Sco), B Koepka (US); -9 D Law (Sco), S Jamieson (Sco), P Harrington (Ire); -8 A Fitzpatrick (Eng), T Fleetwood (Eng); -6 L Donald (Eng), L Westwood (Eng); -5 T Hatton (Eng), J Rose (Eng); -4 I Poulter (Eng)

England's Matthew Jordan is two shots off the lead heading into the final round of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship.

The 30-year-old made a six-under-par 66 to finish the day 16 under, which kept the pressure on leader Casey Jarvis of South Africa.

Poland's Adrian Meronk, who shot the joint-best round of the day with a nine-under 63, is also 16 under.

Belgium's Thomas Detry is a further shot back on 15 under after a seven-under 65 at St Andrews.

Jordan, bidding to win a DP World Tour event, started the third round at Kingsbarns and carded a six-under 66 to move to 16 under.

After finishing as runner-up at the Nexo Championship in Scotland in August, Jordan, who claimed the 2017 St Andrews Links Trophy as an amateur, is keen to go one better on the final day.

"What I wanted to do, and felt like I hadn't done over the last 12, 18 months was put myself in a position to win," Jordan told the DP World Tour., external

"Certainly. I kind of always felt that maybe I was a bit too far back and needed an amazing round to make it happen. I've done well in the last couple events.

"I want to give myself a really good chance. And then just try and win a golf tournament."

Jarvis acknowledged he was "going to be feeling pressure" to hold off the chasing pack in the final round.

"I still know I am going to feel first tee nerves and pressure throughout the day, but I am just going to try and manage it as much as I can," he said.

Jarvis began his round with an eagle at the first and went on to card a bogey-free 65 at St Andrews to move to 18 under.

Meronk made birdies at his opening four holes at Kingsbarns and added an eagle later in his nine-under 63 to join Jordan on 16 under.

England's Matt Fitzpatrick made six under at St Andrews to sit at 12 under alongside defending champion Robert MacIntyre and fellow Scot Calum Hill.

item.title: Gloucester thrash sorry Quins to go top of the Prem
item.description: Gloucester thrash a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm to go to the top of the early Prem standings.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

The Prem

Gloucester (24) 48

Tries: Loader, Morgan, Trenholm, C. Atkinson, S. Atkinson, Englefield, Joseph, Barton Cons: Barton 4

Harlequins (0) 0

Gloucester thrashed a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm to go to the top of the early Prem standings.

The Cherry and Whites ran in eight tries to make it two wins from two in the league and three on the bounce in all competitions.

Gloucester, who named three new signings in their starting line-up including Wales internationals Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, completely outplayed their opponents in all facets of the match.

Visitors Quins, who handed a debut to England full-back George Furbank, struggled to get a handle on the game from the outset and remain bottom of the table without any points after failing to get on the scoreboard.

A progressive move down the right gave Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson – three days after he signed a new deal committing his long-term future with the club - the opportunity to find Ben Loader free on the left with a pinpoint kick, and the winger dotted down to open the scoring.

Harlequins, in their desperation to keep Gloucester out on their own try line, lost Will Evans to the sin bin and mere seconds later Wales flanker Morgan barged over in the left corner to extend Gloucester's lead.

On the stroke of half hour, Morgan's strong carry allowed Will Trenholm to force over Gloucester's third try from close range before George Barton slotted the conversio superbly from touch.

A spectacular 50:22 from scrum-half Caolan Englefield then put Gloucester in another great position and Charlie Atkinson broke a tackle to go over next to the sticks, as Barton kicked an easy extra two to give the hosts a 24-point advantage at half-time.

The interval did not change the momentum as two short passes saw Seb Atkinson race to the line and power over Gloucester's fifth of the evening and Quins' day was perhaps summed up best when Connor Slevin's poor restart failed to go 10 metres.

Gloucester ruthlessly made their visitors pay once more as with their next attack Will Joseph's outstanding run and offload allowed Englefield to dive over.

Joseph then grabbed the try his own performance deserved, diving in to the right of the posts to claim Gloucester's seventh try and third inside 12 minutes after half-time.

Another kick to the corner from Charlie Atkinson found Barton who juggled successfully and managed to extend over for Gloucester's eighth.

Joseph thought he had scored his second with the final act of the match to take Gloucester past 50 points, but his try was chalked off for a knock-on in the build up.

item.title: Glasgow and Ulster play out thrilling draw in URC
item.description: George Horne's late penalty hits the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster play out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Glasgow Warriors (14) 33

Tries: McKay, Rowe 2, Dobie,Talakai Cons: Horne 4

Ulster (19) 33

Tries: B Ward, McIlroy, Murphy, Mullins, Augustus Cons: Murphy 3, Doak

George Horne's late penalty hit the post as Glasgow Warriors and Ulster played out a thrilling 33-33 draw in the United Rugby Championship.

Ulster, seeking their first win in Glasgow in more than five years, led 19-14 at the break but the Warriors scored three tries in a clinical nine-minute spell when Ulster had two players sin-binned to take the lead.

But Glasgow were reduced to 13 inside the final 10 minutes and Juarno Augustus' try, converted by Nathan Doak, levelled the game.

Despite being two players down, Horne had a chance to win the match but his penalty came back off the upright with four minutes left and the points were shared at Scotstoun.

There was blow for Ulster before kick-off as Jacob Stockdale, set to win his 150th cap, was forced out of the starting team in the warm-up but the visitors did not let his withdrawal impact their start.

After being slow out of the blocks at home to Edinburgh in their opener proved costly, Ulster started the better side and took the lead when Bryn Ward barrelled over the line in the fourth minute from a short penalty, and Jack Murphy converted.

But Glasgow, who only lost at home once in the entirety of last season, hit back when Josh McKay rounded off a flowing move, and George Horne added the conversion to level the game.

That handed the Warriors the momentum but the hosts were soon reduced to 14 players when Dan Lancaster was sent to the sin-bin for a deliberate knock on, and Ulster immediately capitalised when Ethan McIlroy darted through a gap to score after building pressure on the home line.

Glasgow responded when Kyle Rowe crossed after a superb pass by centre Stafford McDowall, which took three Ulster players out of the game, and Horne converted to put the hosts into a two-point lead.

There was a final twist in the half when Horne won a penalty after being dragged into a ruck but retaliated by throwing the ball at Ulster hooker Tom Stewart, and the decision was reversed.

Ulster went up the other end and McIlroy's superb offload allowed Murphy to cross in the final play of the half.

The fly-half converted his own score to give Ulster a five-point lead at the break.

Late drama at Scotstoun

Chay Mullins marked his debut by scoring Ulster's bonus-point try just six minutes after the restart after more good work from McIlroy, and Murphy's conversion put the visitors 12 points clear.

But indiscipline cost Ulster as Ben Carson, who was drafted into the team to replace Stockdale, was sent to the sin bin for a high tackle on McDowall and, in the following play, McIlroy was also carded for a deliberate knock on to leave Richie Murphy's side with 13 players.

Glasgow immediately took advantage as Jamie Dobie raced over in the corner after the hosts worked some space, and Horne landed his third conversion of the game.

The hosts were held up over the line from a rolling maul, but they made the most of their momentum when Sam Talakai burrowed over the line to level the game, and Horne nudged Glasgow back in front.

Despite having Carson back on the field, Rowe then raced clear to extend Glasgow's lead after some soft Ulster defence.

But Rory Darge and Talakai were sent to the sin bin inside the final 10 minutes to leave the hosts with 13 after repeated infringements as Ulster camped on the Glasgow line, and Augustus crashed over before Doak levelled the game.

In late drama, Carson was penalised for holding on at a ruck to give Glasgow a kickable penalty but Horne could only hit the upright.

The final minutes were chaotic as both sides threw away possession in search of a decisive score, but Zac Ward was bundled into touch with the clock in the red to ensure the game ended level.

Glasgow Warriors host Connacht on Friday in their third match of the season while Ulster face Munster in Belfast on Saturday.

item.title: Who was the best player on the pitch? - England player ratings
item.description: England produce one of their best performances in recent times as they thump Croatia 6-0 in Rijeka. How did our report rate the players' performances?
item.content:encoded:
• Published

England produced one of their best performances in recent times as they thumped Croatia 7-0 in Rijeka.

Harry Kane opened the scoring, and Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka also found the net before half-time.

England captain Kane then added a fifth early on in the second half before Saka scored his second from close range and substitute Morgan Rogers added a seventh to secure a dominant win.

Here's how BBC Sport England reporter Alex Howell rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.

England starting XI

Jordan Pickford: A really good decision and save when he raced out and won the ball at the feet of Ivan Perisic early on. Not tested but was lucky to not concede with Mateo Kovacic's incredible miss. 6

Jarell Quansah: Surprisingly chosen at right-back over Trent Alexander-Arnold but the Bayer Leverkusen defender does exactly what manager Thomas Tuchel wants. A powerful runner, a good defender and his ability on the ball is underrated - he showed it with a quality assist for Gordon. 8

Ezri Konsa: Not loads of defending for Konsa to do as England pinned Croatia back but it was a calm assured performance from the defender. 7

Marc Guehi: The centre-back had to take up some risky positions as England pressed man for man all over the pitch. 7

Lewis Hall: The Newcastle left-back looks a great addition to the England back four. Hall offers pace going forward and also underlapped, going into midfield to recieve the ball. 7

Elliot Anderson: Anderson has been excellent throughout this international break and produced another mature performance. The Manchester City midfielder is a crucial part of the midfield and set up Kane for England's fifth. 8

Alex Scott: The Bournemouth midfielder was given his first England start and put in a really confident performance. Scott always looked to get on the ball and did not just try to keep it safe as England dominated. 7

Jude Bellingham: The best player on the pitch. Bellingham produced a lovely pass to thread Kane through for the first goal, scored England's second and assisted Saka for England's fourth. A truly world-class player and his quality was too much for Croatia throughout the game. 9

Bukayo Saka: The winger scored twice and looks to be building a good partnership with Quansah on England's right-hand side. Saka could have had a hat-trick but missed a big chance in the second half. 8

Anthony Gordon: Playing with a huge amount of confidence and continues to show that he has gone to another level in recent months. Assisted Bellingham and scored for the fourth England game in a row. 9

Harry Kane: Just an elite finisher and his goal put England firmly in control. The captain looked full of energy, pressed from the front and showed his passing range as he enjoyed having Gordon and Bellingham supplying him. Scored England's fifth goal too. 9

Substitutes

Eberechi Eze (on 70, Gordon): Played as a number 10. 6

Morgan Rogers (on 70, Kane): Played on the left as England cruised to a win and produced a composed finish for England's seventh, rounding the keeper when played through on goal. 7

James Garner (on 70, Alex Scott): Some strong challenges and kept it simple. 6

Morgan Gibbs-White (on 79, Anderson): 6

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on, Hall): 6

Subs not used: Steele, Trafford, Alexander-Arnold, Branthwaite, Calvert-Lewin, Chalobah, Ngumoha.

How did you rate the players?

Player of the match

item.title: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challenge
item.description: Sir Kevin Sinfield crosses the finish line at Old Trafford after seven ultramarathons in seven days.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Sir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.

Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.

The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.

Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."

Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way.

The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.

Along the way he was surprised by royals, including The Prince and Princess of Wales and the Princess Royal, as well as famous names from the sporting world such as former England football manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Leeds boxer Josh Warrington.

Each day was split into 7km, hour-long blocks with an additional extra mile for members of the MND community to join.

Funds raised by the challenge will go towards the work of the MND Association, Leeds Hospitals Charity, My Name5 Doddie Foundation, Darby Rimmer Foundation, MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association.

Sinfield, 45, who played his entire professional career with Leeds Rhinos, is one of the most successful players in Super League history.

He and Burrow met at the Leeds Rhinos academy aged 14 and 12. They went on to win seven titles together with Leeds Rhinos.

Burrow's wife, Lindsey Burrow, told BBC Radio 4's PM that her late husband "would have been incredibly proud" of his friend.

"It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community," Lindsey said.

"It's just incredible. I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years," she added.

Sinfield's son, Jack Sinfield, lined up in the Wakefield side seeking to clinch their first top-flight title since 1968.

item.title: Wu thrashes Trump to set up Yuan final in Shenzhen
item.description: Chinese world champion Wu Yize wins six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 at the Shenzhen Open and set up a final against countryman Yuan Sijun.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Reigning world champion Wu Yize won six consecutive frames to beat Judd Trump 6-1 in the Shenzhen Open semi-finals.

Yize, who will leapfrog Trump in the rankings and move second in the world after the final, bounced back in dramatic fashion after losing the opening frame to set up an all-Chinese final against Yuan Sijun at the Bao'an Sports Centre on Sunday.

Yuan, 26, endured a much more difficult route to his maiden ranking final, battling through 6-5 against Englishman Jimmy Robertson.

World number two Trump, who won the Shanghai Masters in August, had gone into the Shenzhen semi-final in fine form after beating Mark Selby 5-0 in the last eight.

But after clinching the opening frame with a break of 77, the 2019 world champion handed the initiative to his opponent with a string of errors.

Wu, 22, capitalised to avenge a defeat by Trump at the last-four stage in Shanghai earlier this year, making three breaks of 50 or more in a scrappy encounter before clinching victory with a break of 110.

"When I was preparing for the evening match, I saw that Yuan had shed some tears," Wu told World Snooker Tour.

"I believe it is his first ranking final. Hopefully, we can put on a great match for everyone. Of course, I hope I can take the trophy home, but we will both give it everything we have."

An emotional Yuan found it much more difficult to get over the winning line, with the lead continually changing hands throughout the best-of-11 encounter before his opponent forced a deciding frame that took 50 minutes to complete and saw a total of 177 points scored.

Robertson put Yuan in a difficult snooker on the final red and clawed back 41 penalty points before himself being put in a snooker, with Yuan finally clearing to the pink to earn his place in the final of the inaugural event.

"I feel that my first ranking final has come a little bit late," said Yuan, who started the tournament as the world number 33 but will move to the cusp of the top 16 with victory on Sunday.

"Since the pandemic in 2020, the years in between have been quite difficult, and I feel it hasn't been easy. So after all these years, I just hope I can give myself something to show for it."

item.title: Rees-Zammit stars as Bristol power past Northampton
item.description: Louis Rees-Zammit scores a double as Bristol edge past reigning champions Northampton in a pulsating Prem tussle.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

The Prem

Bristol (15) 41

Tries: Oghre, Rees-Zammit 2, Jordan, Randall, Penalty Cons: Williams 3 Pens: Williams

Northampton (14) 26

Tries: Hendy 2, Mitchell, Kemeny Cons: F. Smith 3

Louis Rees-Zammit scored a double as Bristol Bears edged past reigning champions Northampton Saints in a pulsating Prem tussle at Ashton Gate.

Although defences were on top in the first half and chances were limited, the tactical battle and ruthless finishing provided great entertainment as they ran in two tries apiece.

Gabriel Oghre opened the scoring for the hosts following a well-worked line-out move and maul before George Hendy crossed in the corner.

And, after Rees-Zammit's clinical close-range score, Hendy went over again to leave the match finely poised at 15-14 in Bristol's favour at the break.

Unanswered, converted tries from Tom Jordan and Harry Randall gave Bears significant breathing space at 29-14, only for two tries in four minutes from Alex Mitchell and Josh Kemeny to get Saints back in the game at 34-26.

But Bears managed to blunt the Saints attack in the closing stages and sealed the win in the final seconds with a penalty try, awarded after a cynical intervention by Saints full-back Tommy Freeman denied Rees-Zammit a hat-trick.

Following an emotional tribute and minute's applause for Jackie Booy, who died last month, led by her husband and Bristol chairmen Chris, Bears set about marking the occasion in fitting fashion with a stylish display that combined, brilliant defence and scintillating attack.

Oghre's set-piece score gave Bears, who were unceremoniously thrashed 94-33 by Saints last season, a sixth-minute lead that was soon wiped out by Hendy's dart to the corner following a fine set-piece move and pass by captain Fraser Dingwall.

A James Williams penalty restored the lead for the Bears, who then had a sumptuous score ruled out, Randall knocking on in the build up to AJ MacGinty's fine cross kick after great work by Rees-Zammit on the right.

However, Bristol speedster Rees-Zammit's next contribution counted, the winger skipping home into the corner from close range to put his side 15-7 to the good.

But, after a lengthy delay following a nasty looking head injury to Bristol's new England international Benhard Janse van Rensburg, the visitors reduced the half-time deficit to a point when Smith's perfectly timed pass out wide allowed Hendy to double his and his side's first-half try tally.

Impressive Bears stave off Saints

Thankfully, Janse van Rensburg was up and walking around during the break, but his absence did not knock Bears out of their stride on their way to a second successive Prem victory this season.

Tom Jordan stretched over to touch down for the third home try soon after the restart and Williams slotted his third kick of the afternoon to make it 22-14.

A third Saints try was then disallowed following an obstruction, and the sniping Randall then bundled over for a converted try near the posts to further extend the home side's advantage after the Saints defence were sucked in to keep the Bears at bay on the line.

Northampton's quality in attack, showcased so stylishly in their nine-try mauling of Newcastle last time out, could not be contained for long with two tries in four minutes putting them within eight points of their hosts.

A slick move saw Dingwall feed Hendy, who selflessly teed up Mitchell on the inside to go under the posts and Kemeny's try put the visitors within eight points.

Bristol showed no signs of panic as their defence held firm impressively to close out a victory sealed with a last-gasp penalty try.

Bristol: Jordan; Rees-Zammit, Janse van Rensburg, Williams, Ibitoye; AJ MacGinty, Randall; Woolmore, Oghre, Kloska, Rubiolo, Batley, Luatua, Grondona, Harding (capt).

Replacements: Gwilliam, Chawatama, Halliwell, Taylor, Owen, Marmion, Pepper Ivanishvili.

Replacements: Smith, Fischetti, Neculai, Lockett, Chick, Mitchell, Belleau, Pater.

item.title: Desmond targeted by Celtic fan protest at Alfred Dunhill
item.description: Celtic's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond is targeted in a protest at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews as tennis balls were thrown towards him.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Celtic's largest shareholder Dermot Desmond was targeted in a protest at the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews as tennis balls were thrown towards him.

Tennis balls with pictures of the 76-year-old's face scored out were thrown on to the green of the 15th hole of the pro-am competition, with images showing Desmond having to be escorted off the course by security.

The Celtic Fans Collective have since released a statement, along with footage and images of the incident.

It read: "Dermot Desmond has essentially been allowed to run Celtic Football Club whilst using his wealth to hide from supporters and accountability. Fans took the chance today to send a message that this arrangement cannot continue."

Desmond is the largest individual shareholder of the Scottish Premiership club but has been criticised in recent seasons for the club's lack of progress in Europe and underwhelming transfer business.

In the wake of Brendan Rodgers' resignation at the beginning of last season, Desmond blamed the former manager for much of the problems that marred the beginning of the 2025-26 campaign.

Then at Celtic's annual general meeting last November, which had to be abandoned due to fan unrest, Desmond's son Ross read out a statement on his behalf.

He began by defending his father, a "lifelong and passionate" Celtic supporter, and vowed that the board would not be "bullied by aggressive and irrational" criticism.

The Irishman defended then chairman Peter Lawwell and chief executive Michael Nicholson, claiming attempts to "dehumanise and vilify them are shameful".

Desmond went on to criticise a section of fans over a recent incident that led to the Green Brigade ultras group being banned and added: "Those people are bullies."

item.title: Group has 'exploded' after Wales win - Bellamy
item.description: Craig Bellamy says Wales' win over Norway has "thrown a hand grenade" into their Nations League group as they go in search of another victory against Denmark in Cardiff on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Craig Bellamy says Wales' win over Norway has "thrown a hand grenade" into their Nations League group as they go in search of another victory against Denmark in Cardiff on Sunday.

Wales remain bottom of Group A4 despite Thursday's morale-boosting triumph over Norway, though they are level on points with the World Cup quarter-finalists and Denmark at the halfway point in the campaign.

They would take a big step towards avoiding a last-place finish by beating Denmark on Sunday (19:45), and receive a significant boost to their European Championship qualification hopes.

If Wales end their Nations League campaign in third place or higher, they will be a top seed in December's draw for Euro 2028 qualifying.

Bellamy says Portugal will win the group "unless a disaster happens" - but feels the race for the places is wide open after his side shocked Norway.

"I don't know with the way the group's gone now because that [result] has thrown in a hand grenade," he said.

Wales v Denmark

Nations League Group A4

Sunday, 4 October, 19:45 BST

Cardiff City Stadium

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

"Basically, the group's exploded now between the three of us because, obviously, Denmark will look at it and say, well, they didn't expect that, so we all sit on three points apart from Portugal.

"Portugal have run away with this, and they're going to win the group. Now can we really be in the mix with these two heavyweight Scandinavian teams? That's the aim. We'll see where that goes."

Wales came from behind against Norway to register their first Nations League A win across two campaigns in the competition's top tier.

The victory also ended a six-match winless run stretching back to November 2025, with Bellamy admitting after the game that he had been through a "really difficult spell".

Wales will now attempt to build on what was the most notable success of the Bellamy era when they take on a Denmark side ranked 21st in the world.

"We have to perform like we did against Norway," Bellamy added.

"That's all I'm thinking about again - consistency and perform, perform, perform."

Nevertheless, Bellamy acknowledged that he is "definitely conscious" of the importance of finishing above fourth in the group.

"We see [the level when] we're playing against teams who are pot one, so if we don't have to play another pot one, then it's nice," he added.

"It's a real motivation, of course. That would really help us."

More changes to come?

Bellamy regularly makes significant changes to his side regardless of results.

Wales' options are limited in this window, with Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Harry Wilson all absent and David Brooks returning to his club after the opening defeat in Portugal.

Even so, Bellamy says he has no choice but to make alterations to the team that started against Norway as Wales play the final game in this new four-match international window.

"If I could pick the team that started the other night, [I would] all day," he said.

"[But it is] just not possible. I would love to make it possible, but it isn't. One or two didn't come through it.

"So, not giving away the team, of course, but there will be one or two changes because we have to."

Wales take on Denmark for the second time in seven days, having been beaten in dispiriting fashion in the reverse fixture last weekend.

Bellamy "didn't recognise" his team in Copenhagen, adding: "That's not what we do and how we've been when we've been at our best.

"We were too disconnected from front to back. We didn't create the overloads. It was too easy for [Denmark] to press us. Five men could press seven of our players - that's impossible.

"We learned a lot; I learned a lot from Denmark."

item.title: 'I want to discover Manchester' - Olid hunts recommendations
item.description: Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break
item.content:encoded:
• Published

Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break.

The Spaniard replaced Marc Skinner two months ago after leaving Hearts but told BBC Sport that she has been so busy working, she has yet to explore her new home.

Having beaten rivals Liverpool on Saturday, United now have a fortnight's break from action while international play-offs for the World Cup take place and Olid is determined to make the most of it.

"I didn't stop from when I arrived!" she said. "Home, work, home, work. My parents are here, my family are here and now I want to discover Manchester."

United's women's team play most of their home matches at Leigh Sports Village, approximately 12 miles west of central Manchester, while they train on the same site as the men at Carrington in Trafford.

Despite achieving great success in the Scottish Women's Premier League, Olid arrived at United as an unknown quantity in English football.

She experienced a difficult start too, her team losing to London City Lionesses on the opening night of the Women's Super League season before being thrashed 5-0 at home by Chelsea a week later - managing just two shots on target combined in those games.

However, drawing at Arsenal was promising, and now four straight wins across the WSL and League Cup with 18 goals scored suggests her philosophy is starting to get through.

Not that she is satisfied just yet.

"I am so happy for the players - they deserve it," Olid said. "We have started to click in a lot of things and they fight for each other.

"But there is still a lot to improve. We created chances, but our last pass and our finishing needs to be better. That will come."

Liverpool counterpart Gareth Taylor was less impressed with Olid's tactics, having seen his side's encouraging start to the season stunted by two defeats in their past three.

"They were very direct and we fell into their trap," Taylor said. "Their goalkeeper was literally kicking out of her hands.

"We have got to be braver and there are lessons to learn. This was the first time where we have not been a good reflection of ourselves."

item.title: Dragons celebrate derby success against Scarlets
item.description: Dragons secure a Welsh derby win in a United Rugby Championship (URC) 10-try thrilling encounter at Rodney Parade in Newport.
item.content:encoded:
• Published

United Rugby Championship

Dragons (12) 38

Tries: Tuitavuki, Dee 2, Martinez, Anderson, Hunt Cons: de Beer 3, J Lloyd

Scarlets (14) 26

Tries: Page 2, S O'Connor, I Jones Cons: Costelow 3

Dragons secured a Welsh derby win in the United Rugby Championship (URC), beating Scarlets in a thrilling 10-try encounter at Rodney Parade.

Two tries from Wales hooker Elliot Dee,and further scores from wing Anzelo Tuitavuki, props Rodrigo Martinez and Rob Hunt and full-back Huw Anderson sealed the six-try success.

Scarlets responded with two tries from wing Macs Page and scores from replacements Sam O'Connor and Ioan Jones.

The match was played in front of a raucous crowd of 7,163 that created a memorable occasion in Newport.

Dragons are unbeaten, following up the opening weekend draw with Benetton, while Scarlets, who are missing influential injured back-row duo Taine Plumtree and Fletcher Anderson, have suffered two derby defeats, having also lost at home to Cardiff.

Scarlets score first as they lead at half-time

Wales fly-half Sam Costelow was among five personnel changes from the Scarlets team that lost 21-15 defeat to Cardiff, with Wales props Kemsley Mathias and Harri O'Connor, lock Alex Groves and flanker Dan Davis starting.

Dragons co-captain Ben Carter returned to lead the side that drew 19-19 with Benetton, but fellow skipper Angus O'Brien was still missing.

Dee, Hunt, and back-row duo Shane Lewis-Hughes and Harri Keddie were also included.

Scrum-half Rhodri Williams led the side out with his family on his 150th Dragons appearance against his former team, where he spent five seasons.

The two teams ran out to easily the most fervent atmosphere of a Welsh home match so far this season, with the fixture benefiting from its sunny Saturday afternoon kick-off time.

It was the away fans who were celebrating first as Page scored a superb solo try after drifting around the Dragons defence before collecting his own chip.

The hosts responded with a period of pressure that was rewarded with a first Dragons try for Tongan wing Tuitavuki.

This inspired the hosts as they kept up the pressure with a well-worked line-out between centre Aneurin Owen and flanker Thomas Young, which laid the platform for another attacking set-piece that yielded a driving try for Dee.

Scarlets scrum-half Dane Blacker sought to install some tempo in the visitors' play, and an attacking scrum allowed centre Eddie James to burst through the middle, before a long Costelow floated pass released Page to stroll in for his second.

Costelow converted as Scarlets led 14-12 at half-time.

Dragons dominate second half to seal win

Dragons struck straight after the break when wing Rio Dyer took the ball superbly from kick-off to put the hosts on the front foot.

After subtle build-up work from de Beer and Anderson, a searing Tuitavuki break was only halted by a brilliant tap tackle from Scarlets full-back Blair Murray, but Argentina prop Martinez followed up to cross, with de Beer converting.

Scarlets retaliated and, following another midfield charge from James, a perfect Page chip narrowly eluded Mee's hands as he lost possession over the Dragons line.

The home side brought on Wales props Rhodri Jones and Dillon Lewis as the duo forced a scrum penalty.

Scarlets replacement prop Sam O'Connor made his own early impression when he burrowed over for the third try.

Costelow's conversion regained the lead, but Scarlets put themselves under pressure with needless penalties from the kick-off.

Dragons flanker Young was held up over the line but it was Anderson who scored the bonus-point try in the right-hand corner to give the Dragons the advantage once more.

Dyer produced an excellent break, and Scarlets captain Josh Macleod could only stop the momentum with a professional foul that resulted in a yellow card.

The hosts took control with Dee driven over for his second score, which proved his final act before being replaced.

Scarlets, playing with 14 men, struck back quickly with a quick line-out before replacement Jones crossed for the bonus-point try.

Dragons gathered themselves and Hunt's final try sealed the success in what was a fourth try on the day for the home front-row.

Line-ups

Replacements: Coghlan, R Jones, Lewis, Woodman, Beddall, Hope, J Lloyd, Paea.

Referee: Adam Jones (WRU)
